subject: D9: whether a reference resolves must not depend on how many resolved before it. GREEN AND EMPTY as of Step 9b.2, and still fail-closed in both directions -- a row appearing here is a behaviour change and fails the run. It was REGISTERED RED from Stage 0a.8 until 9b.2 with two rows, both of which cleared in the commit that made a reference a node.
purpose:
Resolving a reference USED TO COPY the definition's destination and title into the node, so markdown_core_map_lookup carried a running budget -- max(100000, input size) bytes summed over successful lookups -- and stopped resolving once it was spent. Two properties died:

  uniform      200 references to one label are identical, so all 200 must resolve or none must. 100 resolved and 100 degraded to text. The split moved with the destination's length; that it split at all was the defect.
  independent  `[b]: /short` then `[b]` resolves. Prefix that document with an unrelated `[a]` whose destination spends the budget and the identical `[b]` became Text literal="[b]". The contamination crossed labels, which is what made it a resolution defect rather than a size limit.

DELETING THE BUDGET WAS NEVER THE FIX, and that is why this was pinned rather than repaired for eleven steps. Measured with the guard removed and nothing in its place: `reference_expansion_bound` in packages/markdown-core/tests/runners/complexity_runner.c went from 0.999x to 204.678x -- 656 KB of input producing 134 MB of copied destinations. The budget bought a linear output bound by breaking resolution; the two gates state both halves, and neither may be satisfied by giving up the other.

A reference that NAMES its definition instead of copying it buys both at once, and that is Step 9b.2: LinkReference and ImageReference carry an association and no destination, the reference map holds labels and no resource, so there is nothing to charge and no budget to break resolution. Both rows cleared and reference_expansion_bound measures 0.399x on the same input -- now counting the association bytes the tree actually stores, so it cannot pass by measuring a field the model no longer has.
